The One Big Beautiful Bill’s wage claims ignore its $5.8 trillion deficit bomb. Yes, tax cuts for workers matter—but this 1,000-page monstrosity is packed with lobbyist handouts and rushed provisions that’ll backfire.

Real reform requires splitting it into targeted bills with enforceable spending caps, not bundling debt hikes with vague promises. The $1.6 trillion in cuts? A drop in the bucket compared to the $6 trillion needed to fix Biden’s mess.

Protect paychecks, yes—but not by mortgaging America’s future on D.C.’s same old tricks.

The One Big Beautiful Bill’s elimination of rigid staffing mandates is a step toward freeing rural providers from D.C.’s bureaucratic stranglehold—but let’s not confuse regulatory relief with real fiscal reform. While scrapping one-size-fits-all rules helps clinics like Richardton operate, the bill’s $700B Medicaid cuts risk destabilizing the very facilities it claims to help.

Rural hospitals survive on Medicaid—slashing reimbursements while trimming red tape is like removing handcuffs before pushing someone off a cliff. True reform requires cutting bloated contracts with billing middlemen and Pharma giants, not essential care funding.

Fix the waste, not the safety net.

The $50B Rural Health Transformation Program sounds noble—until you peel back the layers. Created under H.R.1 (the Big Beautiful Bill), this initiative funnels cash through state bureaucracies instead of directly empowering rural hospitals. Half the funds get split evenly whether states deliver results or not, while CMS dangles the rest as discretionary pork.

Meanwhile, the same bill slashes $155B from rural Medicaid over a decade—starving the very communities this program claims to help. Classic D.C. math: throw billions at new bureaucracies while gutting existing safety nets.

Real transformation requires patient-centered solutions, not more middlemen.

See how the numbers and fine print expose the real impact behind the headlines: https://t.co/HM3iGmMCOH
